title: Zephyrine and the Parish
premise: True-crime podcaster Marguerite Winterbourne has spent three years quietly documenting the unsolved disappearance of Father Ambrose Zephyrine, the beloved parish priest who vanished from St. Aldhelm's in 1971. When a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after a parishioner's funeral, Marguerite realizes someone alive knows what happened—and that her own archive has been read by eyes other than hers. As she follows the letter's clues through sealed parish records and the memories of aging congregants, she discovers the killer is someone embedded in her investigation, using her podcast to monitor how close she's getting. In the end, Marguerite stages a final episode as bait, forcing a confrontation in the church crypt where the truth about Zephyrine—a man killed for threatening to expose the parish's financial rot—finally surfaces, and she must choose between publishing the story that will make her career and protecting the innocent family entangled in the old sin.
about_author: J. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former parish archivist from the English Midlands who spent a decade cataloguing church records before turning to fiction. Their debut draws on a lifetime of listening to confessions that were never meant for them.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet her in her cluttered home office, filing the last notes on episode forty-seven of 'Cold Parish,' her podcast on Father Zephyrine's 1971 vanishing. Establishes her obsessive order, her loneliness, and her rule never to get involved. Emotional beat: controlled detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A handwritten confession arrives—one day after the funeral of Edith Marsh, the last living witness—with details only the killer could know. The postmark terrifies her: whoever sent it was at the funeral, watching. Emotional beat: dread; her safe distance collapses.

chapters.title: What Edith Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with flashback passages from Edith's letters. Searching Edith's estate sale boxes, Marguerite finds a torn photograph of Zephyrine with three young parishioners—one face scratched out. Emotional beat: grief braided with the first thrill of pursuit.

chapters.title: The Vestry Locks Its Doors
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Marguerite and Father Callum Reeve, the young priest newly assigned to St. Aldhelm's, who blocks her access to the parish archive. His evasiveness reads as either guilt or protection. Emotional beat: suspicion; an uneasy alliance forms over shared tea and mutual distrust.

chapters.title: A Second Letter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A second letter arrives quoting her own podcast verbatim—including an unedited detail she never aired. Someone has been inside her files. She realizes the killer isn't following the case; they're following her. Emotional beat: violation and paranoia.

chapters.title: The Money in the Walls
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Digging into restoration ledgers, Callum uncovers decades of siphoned building-fund money tied to a founding family—the Ashcombes—whose scion, Gerald Ashcombe, funds the parish generously to this day. Emotional beat: dawning horror that the corruption never ended.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She interviews the surviving trio from the photograph; two lie fluently, one weeps. The scratched-out face belongs to Gerald Ashcombe's late father. Her producer warns the new episodes are drawing legal threats. Emotional beat: the cost of belonging—she's no longer invisible, and it's dangerous.

chapters.title: The Episode That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Discovering her office was searched, Marguerite decides to weaponize the leak: she records a fake finale claiming she's found Zephyrine's remains and will reveal the location next week. Emotional beat: cold resolve; hunter becomes bait.

chapters.title: Crypt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, converging. On release night, someone breaks into the crypt—and so does Marguerite, with Callum and police nearby. The killer is revealed: Edith Marsh's grandson, a parish warden raised on the Ashcombe secret, confessing he killed to keep his grandmother's complicity buried. Physical struggle; Zephyrine's true fate surfaces—he was murdered for threatening to expose the theft. Emotional beat: terror breaking into truth.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, weeks later. The arrest made, she faces the choice: air the full story and destroy the parish that sheltered the innocent alongside the guilty, or soften it. She publishes everything—but ends the series by reading Edith's original letters aloud, giving the town its grief back. Callum asks her to stay. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; love against duty resolved.
